Kuvitus: talvinen pulkkamäki. Mäen huipu: Illustration: a winter sledding hill. Two children stand at the top of the hill, and one child's sled waits to start. The left slope of the hill is steep and short, the right slope gentle and long, and a flat snow field continues from the foot of each slope. On both sides the tracks of the sled run down the slope and along the flat to a sled that has stopped with a child at a red marker flag. On the left the sled that came down the steep side has slid far along the flat, on the right the sled from the gentle side only a little, and both flags are equally far from the top of the hill measured horizontally. In the background are a forest, a red cottage and snowy mounds. The height of the hill and the distances are to scale, the children and sleds larger.
Kolme tilannetta. Ylhäällä tilannekuvat: Three situations. At the top are situation pictures and below the dashed line free-body diagrams in which the chosen body is a rectangle and the forces are to scale inside each diagram. On the left a lift starts up: a person stands on the floor of the lift car, and a blue velocity arrow points up. In the person's free-body diagram the weight G from the centre down and the normal force N of the floor from the bottom surface up, longer than the weight, and an orange acceleration arrow up. In the middle a skydiver descends under a parachute at a steady speed: a velocity arrow down. In the free-body diagram the weight G down and the air resistance F_v from the top surface up, equally long, acceleration zero. On the right a sled slides down a slope to the left: a velocity arrow down the slope. In the free-body diagram the sled is a rectangle tilted along the slope: the weight G from the centre straight down, the normal force N from the bottom surface perpendicularly out of the slope and the kinetic friction F_mu from the upper corner of the bottom surface up the slope, short. The acceleration arrow down the slope.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: pulkka läht: Schematic, not to scale: a sled starts from rest at the top of a hill, slides down a straight slope and continues along the flat until it stops. The length of the slope is L and its height h, and the slope is at an angle alpha to the horizontal. The horizontal length of the slope is x 1, that is, L times the cosine of alpha, and on the flat the sled slides a distance x 2. In both places the sled is drawn at rest, speed zero.
Vasemmalla tilannekuva: pulkka ja lapsi: On the left a situation picture: a sled and a child slide down a snowy slope to the left, and a blue velocity arrow above the sled points down the slope. The slope rises to the right at an angle of 20 degrees. On the right the free-body diagram of the sled, the sled as a rectangle tilted along the slope, forces to scale. The weight G from the centre straight down. The normal force N from the bottom surface perpendicularly out of the slope, a little shorter than the weight. The kinetic friction F_mu from the upper corner of the bottom surface up the slope, short. The components of the weight as dashed lines from the centre: G x down the slope, longer than the friction, and G y perpendicularly towards the slope. Separately an orange acceleration arrow down the slope. In the corner the axes: x down the slope and y perpendicularly out of the slope.
Mallikuvio. Vasemmalla tilannekuva: hiss: Model diagram. On the left a situation picture: a lift car with a spring scale hanging from its ceiling and a suitcase on the hook of the scale. The lift moves down and accelerates. On the right the free-body diagram of the suitcase, the suitcase as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre down and the tension T of the scale from the top surface up, shorter than the weight. Separately a blue velocity arrow down and an orange acceleration arrow down. They are not forces.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, keksitty esimerkk: Graph to scale, invented example data: the reading N of a force-sensor plate in newtons as a function of time, when a student of 60.0 kilograms stands on the plate in a lift moving upwards. On the horizontal axis time 0 to 14 seconds, on the vertical axis force 0 to 700 newtons at intervals of 50 newtons. Until 1.0 s the reading is about 589 newtons. From 1.0 s to 3.0 s the reading is 650 newtons. From 3.0 s to 9.0 s the reading is again about 589 newtons. From 9.0 s to about 12.2 s the reading is 550 newtons, and after that again about 589 newtons.

Graph to scale, invented example data: the reading N of a force-sensor plate in newtons as a function of time, when a person of 75.0 kilograms stands on the plate in a lift moving downwards. On the horizontal axis time 0 to 10 seconds, on the vertical axis force 0 to 900 newtons at intervals of 50 newtons. Until 1.0 s the reading is about 736 newtons. From 1.0 s to 3.0 s the reading is 650 newtons. From 3.0 s to 6.0 s the reading is again about 736 newtons. From 6.0 s to about 8.7 s the reading is 800 newtons, and after that again about 736 newtons.
